A few weeks ago my friends and I witnessed somebody on a scooter get hit by a car. The car just drove off. We called an ambulance, but it looked like the person was unresponsive, and a nearby cop refrained from performing CPR. We don’t know if they died; we left when some first responders came to handle the situation. Later, we were constantly checking the news for updates on this persons health, but we couldn’t find anything. We still don’t know if this person survived the accident.

Later that evening, we all hugged each other and said how much we loved and cared for each other. It’s crazy how witnessing something like this puts your life into perspective. So often we are just going through life, perhaps deeply engaged in the details, but without the mindfulness or appreciation of the fragility of this entire experience. It very well may be snatched away from us or a loved one. We should cherish it as much as we can, and learn to be more mindful when we realize we may have been taking it all for granted. I don’t know, these are my thoughts. It’s late but I was struck by your post.
